power_Monitoring: add a power_ServodWrapper loop-runner This change introduces power_Monitoring, a test that runs tests in a specified suite wrapped with power_ServodWrapper for a given amount of time. The test ensures the DUTs do not run out of power by using v4's power management to keep the DUTs always above a specified threshold. It charges the DUT in those cases to an upper threshold before continuining the tests. As a demonstration vehicle, this CL adds power_LoadTest.1hour to the suite. A subsequent CL adds the first batch of tests to this runner BUG=chromium:923765 TEST=manual testing test_that --autotest_dir=[...] $DUT_IP power_Monitoring observe as tests start looping Change-Id: Ib147f127fbb70730716960d2a997fd6a4a73fb36 Signed-off-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1423938 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>

firmware_Cr50OpenWhileAPOff: add workaround for broken rdd Some boards can't detect Rdd disconnect when the EC is off. If CCD_MODE_L is deasserted, then cr50 will disable ccd even if it thinks rdd is connected. In 4.19, we can start setting CCD_MODE_L using gpioset. Use gpioset to deassert CCD_MODE_L to disable ccd instead of just relying on servo_v4_dts_mode:off. This will allow us to run the test on more boards. We aren't testing Rdd with this test. We just need cr50 to be able to enter deep sleep and cr50 can't unless ccd is disabled. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=run on atlas with dev signed 4.19. Make sure the test passes. Run with 3.18 and make sure it still fails with TEST_NA. chromeos-cr50-scripts: cr50 event log tracking script The new script is invoked once after startup. First the script updates the Cr50 flash log time base, so that new events would be reported with the correct time stamp. The time stamp of the most recent reported event is saved in /mnt/stateful_partition/unencrypted/preserve/cr50_flog_timestamp which makes sure that it survives powerwashes, OS updates, etc. If the file does not exist, it is created with the value of time stamp of 0. The script polls the Cr50 to retrieve log entries added after the most recent reported one. If there are such entries, their timestamp is saved and the event ID is added to the sparse UMA histogram Platform.Cr50.FlashLog, and after successful addition the time stamp is saved as the BRANCH=none BUG=b:132287488 TEST=generated a few log entries using Cr50 console command and ran the script. Observed the entries showing up in chrome://histograms and verified that the timestamps are matching real time. Verified that there are no duplicate histogram updates when this script is re-ran, and that new events show up in the histogram if they are added on the Cr50. Verified that when running on a DUT with Cr50 version not yet supporting flash log, cr50-metrics.conf still completes successfully. Change-Id: Iae47fe015e0fb41f6ff165f4db9f5bdbe53c1bfc Signed-off-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1649196 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Namyoon Woo <namyoon@chromium.org>

cheets_{CTS,GTS}: Fail if the test count was not a multiple of abi count. CTS/GTS runs against multiple ABIs that the device supports. For instance if a device supports x86 and x86_64, then it runs each test case twice, once as x86 ABI and another as x86_64. Thus, the total test count should become a multiple of the ABI count. This is a hack to detect b/133420179 that runs only 151 test cases when 151*2 = 302 is required, abusing the fact that 151 is an odd number.
